title: British fort built on Tiwi Country
detail: Fort Dundas, the first British fort in northern Australia, on Melville Island; abandoned in 1828 after Tiwi resistance, cyclones and tropical conditions.

title: British fort at Port Essington
detail: Fort Victoria built on Iwaidja Country on the Cobourg Peninsula in October 1838; abandoned in December 1849.

title: South Australia claims the Territory
detail: Letters patent place Aboriginal Country under South Australia, opening it to survey and sale.

title: Palmerston (Darwin) built on Larrakia Country
detail: Surveyor-General George Goyder establishes a settlement of 135 colonists.

title: Daly River massacre
detail: After four miners were killed at the Mt Hayward copper mine, police (Mounted Constable George Montagu, Inspector Paul Foelsche) and a civilian party led reprisals against Malak Malak, Woolwonga and Murrinh-patha people. Official estimate 20-30 dead; the Protector of Aborigines said 'not less than 150'.
source_title: Colonial Frontier Massacres map, Daly River

title: Jampawurru (Red Lily Spring) massacre
detail: Seven or eight Aboriginal men killed by a party including Gordon Buchanan.

title: Police killings at Corella and Cresswell Downs
detail: Police-led expedition at Corella and Cresswell Downs after two settlers were killed; Aboriginal people killed, number unrecorded.

title: Northern Territory Aboriginals Act
detail: The Chief Protector becomes 'legal guardian of every Aboriginal and every half-caste child up to the age of 18 years'.

title: Commonwealth takes over; Chief Protector's powers
detail: On 1 January 1911 the Commonwealth takes control of the NT. Its Ordinance gives the Chief Protector 'the care, custody or control of any Aboriginal or half caste'. These powers last until 1957.

title: Kahlin Compound opens
detail: Compound outside Darwin; girls kept in dormitories described as 'like birds in a cage'.

title: The Bungalow opens in Stuart (Alice Springs)
detail: Removals of light-skinned children from Aboriginal camps begin.

title: Aboriginals Ordinance 1918
detail: The Chief Protector controls Aboriginal women 'from the moment they were born until they died', unless married to a man 'substantially of European origin'. In 1997 the High Court held (Kruger) that the Ordinance did not authorise genocide as the Convention defines it.

title: Half-Caste Home opens in Darwin
detail: Separates Compound families.

title: Coniston massacre
detail: Reprisal raids led by Constable George Murray after Frederick Brooks was killed at Yurrkuru. The Board of Enquiry found 31 Aboriginal people killed and said the party acted in self-defence; historians estimate at least double. The Board heard no Aboriginal witnesses except tracker Paddy and Aboriginal people had no counsel.

title: Coniston Board of Enquiry clears police
detail: Found the killings justified as self-defence, with evidence not made public.

title: Bleakley report
detail: Estimates about 8,000 'half-castes' among roughly 21,000 Aboriginal people; finds institutions 'badly situated, inadequately financed and insufficiently supervised'.

title: 132 children at The Bungalow
detail: Then at Temple Bar.

title: McEwen's 'New Deal'
detail: Increases government control over people of mixed descent; Half-Caste Home inmates moved to Bagot Compound.

title: Children evacuated south after Darwin is bombed
detail: Mission children sent to homes in SA, NSW and Victoria.

title: Retta Dixon Home opens
detail: Opens after the war with 51 children, later peaking at 120; operates until 1980.

title: Removal age instructions
detail: Instructions limit removal of children under four, later lowered to three months.

title: Welfare Ordinance 1953
detail: Repeals the 1918 Ordinance; the Director of Welfare becomes guardian of all 'wards'. A 1953 inquiry calls Retta Dixon 'a failure'.

title: Southern fostering scheme
detail: The Commonwealth begins sending part-Aboriginal children to foster homes and schools in southern states, until the late 1960s.

title: Register of Wards gazetted
detail: 15,711 Aboriginal Territorians named as wards; only six full-descent people left off, including Albert Namatjira. Barry Christophers called it 'an instrument of torture against the Aborigines'.

title: Social Welfare Ordinance
detail: Reserve entry limited to people 'socially or economically in need of assistance'.

title: Equal wage decision deferred
detail: Equal wages for Aboriginal stockmen were decided but deferred three years after pastoralists said it would ruin the industry.
state_account: Pastoralists: equal pay would ruin the industry.

title: Wave Hill walk-off
detail: On 23 August 1966 about 200 Gurindji stockmen and families, led by Vincent Lingiari, walk off Wave Hill station.

title: 18% of Aboriginal children in government care
detail: Almost 18% of Territory Indigenous children in government care in 1967-68.

title: Equal wages take effect
detail: Paying Aboriginal workers more than a set amount in goods and money had been illegal until 1968.

title: 97% of children in foster care Indigenous
Assimilation policy formally abandoned
detail: Policy shifts from assimilation to self-management. Bilingual education begins in NT schools around this time (date to confirm).

title: Whitlam hands land back to the Gurindji
detail: On 16 August 1975 Gough Whitlam pours soil into Vincent Lingiari's hands.

title: Aboriginal Land Rights (NT) Act
detail: Passed 16 December 1976, operating from 26 January 1977; creates the land councils.

title: CDEP begins
detail: Community Development Employment Projects, run by communities (start year to confirm).
source_title: Northern Land Council, Submission 493, racism inquiry (2026)

title: NT Government takes control
detail: The Commonwealth hands the Territory to an NT Legislative Assembly with a Chief Minister.

title: Karu Aboriginal child care agency founded
First move to end bilingual education
detail: The NT moved to end bilingual education in 1980, 1998, 2008 and 2024, never consulting communities first.

title: Child Placement Principle enters NT law
detail: The Community Welfare Act is the first NT law to include the Aboriginal Child Placement Principle.

title: Age of criminal responsibility set at 10
detail: Under the NT Criminal Code (year to confirm).

title: Royal Commission into Aboriginal Deaths in Custody begins
detail: Announced 10 August 1987; examined 99 deaths from 1980 to 1989.

title: Bilingual education at its peak
detail: 21 schools in 17 languages.

title: Royal Commission final report
detail: Signed 15 April 1991 with 339 recommendations.

title: Mandatory sentencing for property offences
detail: Introduced 1997, repealed 2001 (dates to confirm against legislation).

title: Kruger v Commonwealth
detail: NT Stolen Generations plaintiffs lose; the High Court holds the 1918 Ordinance did not authorise genocide as the Convention defines it.

title: Bringing Them Home
detail: Finds forced-removal policies fell within the international definition of genocide.
actor: Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission

title: Second move to end bilingual education
Nulyarimma v Thompson
detail: Federal Court holds 2:1 that genocide is not a crime in Australian law without legislation; Merkel J dissents.

title: Genocide offence with Attorney-General's consent gate
detail: Division 268 of the Criminal Code from 1 September 2002; any prosecution needs the Attorney-General's written consent (s 268.121).
state_account: Consent is standard for universal-jurisdiction crimes.

title: The Intervention
detail: Announced 21 June 2007, legislated in August. Income management, alcohol and pornography bans, compulsory five-year leases, suspended permits, CDEP abolished, extra police with army support. The Racial Discrimination Act exemption ran until 2010; only two of the 97 Little Children are Sacred recommendations were implemented.
what_it_takes: Control of money, land and movement

title: CDEP abolished
detail: Replaced with work for the dole, which NLC chair Matthew Ryan calls 'modern slavery'. Under CDEP people 'were happier and healthy in the homelands and the community'.
source_title: Northern Land Council, Submission 493, racism inquiry (2026)

title: Compulsory five-year leases
detail: Over township land in prescribed communities.

title: Racial Discrimination Act exemption ends
detail: UN Special Rapporteur James Anaya finds the measures racially discriminatory.

title: Hearing loss among prisoners
detail: 94% of Aboriginal inmates tested in Darwin and Alice Springs prisons had significant hearing loss; most did not know.

title: Stronger Futures
detail: The 2007 Act is replaced on 16 July 2012 by Stronger Futures, keeping many measures.

title: 'Effective enrolment' funding
detail: Funding follows attendance, not need; a Deloitte review found it flowed to mostly non-Aboriginal, urban students. Aboriginal students lost about $3,000 each a year against $340 for non-Aboriginal students.

title: Aboriginal attendance 68.2%
detail: Start of the steepest fall in four decades of data.

title: Community Development Program
detail: Over 50,000 financial penalties in one three-month period (start year to confirm).

title: Homelands handed to the NT
detail: Commonwealth transfers homelands responsibility to the NT; leaders call it a 'backroom deal'.

title: Four Corners 'Australia's Shame'
detail: Aired 25 July 2016, showing abuse in Don Dale; a Royal Commission is called within days.
source_title: Royal Commission into the Protection and Detention of Children in the NT (Wikipedia)

title: Royal Commission reports
detail: Tabled 17 November 2017: 142 findings and 226 recommendations, describing a 'constant roundabout' of school disengagement, court and placement breakdown.
source_title: Royal Commission into the Protection and Detention of Children in the NT (Wikipedia)

title: Spit hoods banned for children
detail: Following the Royal Commission.

title: NT Aboriginal Ranger Grants begin
detail: Pays for ranger equipment, facilities and training.

title: Alcohol floor price
detail: $1.30 minimum unit price introduced.

title: Public drinking decriminalised
detail: Reform made in line with the Deaths in Custody Royal Commission.

title: Kumanjayi Walker shot in Yuendumu
detail: The coroner later described some evidence of racism and violence in NT Police as deeply disturbing. Officer Zachary Rolfe had served five years in the Army.

title: 23 Aboriginal people a day into custody
detail: January 2020 average.

title: Floor price evaluation
detail: Menzies found a 14% fall in alcohol-related assaults and a 21% fall in alcohol-related family violence assaults after three years.
state_account: The CLP later cited a 38% rise in assaults.

title: 60.3% return to prison within two years
detail: People released in 2021-22; highest in Australia (national 43.0%).

title: 54% of remote houses overcrowded
detail: National Audit Office report.

title: $2,703.68 per child per day
detail: Cost of youth detention in 2022-23, about $987,000 a year.

title: Courts adjourn for lack of interpreters
detail: Interpreters employed fell by almost half over a decade; most of 170 registered are casual. One NAAJA client spent nearly two weeks on remand, his case adjourned three times.

title: Kalkarindji and Daguragu flood evacuation
detail: About 700 people evacuated to Howard Springs for up to two months; Pigeon Hole residents still in tents three months on.

title: Age of criminal responsibility raised to 12
detail: Under the previous Labor government (date to confirm).

title: Age lowered back to 10; Declan's Law
detail: Age of criminal responsibility lowered from 12 to 10; bail tightened with electronic monitoring for repeat offenders.

title: Public drinking offence returns
detail: Police can fine up to $925, issue a seven-day Banned Drinker Order and arrest, then check for warrants and bail breaches.

title: Holtze becomes the only youth detention centre
detail: 30 km from Darwin, no public transport; Alice Springs children moved there.
source_title: Justice not Jails, Submission 282, racism inquiry (2026)

title: 40 Aboriginal people a day into custody
detail: From December 2024, nearly double the 2020 average.

title: $4 billion remote housing agreement
detail: 10-year Commonwealth-NT deal for up to 2,700 homes; Commonwealth share $2.1B.
state_account: Largest remote housing investment in NT history.

title: Bilingual funding cut, then reversed
detail: NT moved to cancel $2.12M of targeted bilingual funding (a quarter of one per cent of the education budget), reversed after ATESOL NT and ACTA objected.

title: Darwin's only rehab and sobering-up shelter closes
detail: Mission Australia facility at Berrimah closed mid-2024 under the previous Labor government to make way for a women's prison; about 40 people in long-term rehab.

title: Every audited child in youth justice known to child protection
detail: NT Children's Commissioner audit; 94% exposed to domestic or family violence.

title: Floor price scrapped
detail: Despite objections from Danila Dilba, Congress, AMSANT, Larrakia Nation and the AMA.
state_account: Assaults rose 38% under the floor price (no source given).

title: Last-resort principle removed for custody
detail: Bail and Youth Justice amendments remove the last-resort principle for custody on arrest and remand.

title: Spit hoods reinstated
detail: Youth Justice amendments: detention no longer a last resort, spit hoods back, wider use-of-force powers.

title: Aboriginal adults 2.07 times more likely to be refused bail
detail: Than similarly placed non-Aboriginal adults (1.64 times for police bail). Over 3,300 people refused bail January-August 2025.

title: 82% of detained children unsentenced
detail: Of 161 children held April-June 2025.

title: 41% of prisoners on remand
detail: November 2025; 52% unsentenced in Darwin Correctional Centre.
source_title: Justice not Jails, Submission 282, racism inquiry (2026)

title: 95% of detained children Aboriginal
detail: 57 of 60 on 6 August 2025.

title: Programs cancelled inside
detail: In six months to March 2025, 10 of 11 drug and alcohol sessions and 34 of 46 psycho-educational programs cancelled.

title: Ranger grants dropped
detail: $12M four-year program left out of the 2025 budget despite a CLP election promise; the budget gave corrections a record $495M.
state_account: Funding had run out; the Commonwealth is the main funder.

title: Territory Coordinator Act
detail: Passed 19 March 2025 over opposition from all four land councils, Larrakia Nation, APO NT and Nurrdalinji.
state_account: Major projects bring jobs and growth.

title: Kumanjayi White dies after police restraint
detail: 24-year-old Warlpiri man with disabilities under state care, restrained by two plain-clothes officers in an Alice Springs supermarket. The DPP declined to prosecute; inquest set for April 2027.

title: Pepper spray legal for the public
detail: One-year trial from 1 September 2025.

title: Parents referred to income management
detail: From October 2025 for persistent absence; 292 fines and 1,398 notices issued in 2025.

title: Schools reach Aboriginal students 54.7% of the time
detail: Against 84.9% for non-Aboriginal students; 40.0% in very remote schools.

title: Effective enrolment ends
detail: Only under Commonwealth funding conditions.

title: Push to redirect NAAJA funding
detail: The Chief Minister proposed moving some NAAJA funding to Legal Aid NT. NAAJA says the NT contributes nothing to its legal services.

title: Badari: High Court strikes down Remote Rent Framework
detail: For denying tenants procedural fairness; the NT then amended the Housing Act so the Minister can set rent without consulting tenants.

title: Woman dies in Tennant Creek watch house
detail: 44-year-old Aboriginal woman; a week later the cause was undetermined.

title: RJED replaces CDP
detail: Up to 3,000 jobs, $707M, plus the Remote Australia Employment Service from 1 November 2025.

title: 60 children flown from Alice Springs to Darwin
detail: In 10 months, all Aboriginal, 10 girls, 16 with or being assessed for disability. Held in an adult transfer facility, handcuffed on commercial flights; families sometimes not told.
state_account: No legislative requirement to notify families.

title: Average youth remand 56 days
detail: One child aged 10-14 spent 238 days on remand before charges were dropped.
source_title: ABC: NAAJA youth justice submission (3 Feb 2026)

title: Remand without conviction
detail: Children 10-13 are presumed incapable of criminal intent, yet youth remand rose from 92 to 133 in a year while sentenced detention fell from 33 to 28.

title: Every Child Matters Act
detail: Passed July 2026: the Child Placement Principle applies only 'as far as practicable'; protection orders capped at two years in favour of permanency; family's right to identify placement removed.
state_account: The principle is restructured, not removed.

title: Only 16.7% placed with kin
detail: About 90% of children in care are Aboriginal; lowest kin placement rate in Australia.

title: 93% of out-of-home care money to providers
detail: $133.2M of $143.4M paid to non-government providers rather than family carers.

title: 4,515 per 100,000 Aboriginal adults imprisoned
detail: June quarter 2026; national Aboriginal rate 2,719.

title: $525M corrections vs $4.9M diversion
detail: 2026/27 budget, about 100 to 1; two work camps $238M.
state_account: Community safety; victims of crime fell 10.2%.
source_title: AAP via Shepparton News: NT budget 2026/27

title: Income management extended to 2033
detail: Self-repeal dates removed despite Labor's 2022 promise to abolish compulsory income management; condemned by the Central Land Council.
state_account: Protects money for food, rent and bills.

title: YiSSA short-stay shelter closes
detail: Darwin's largest short-stay shelter, run by Yilli Rreung Housing Aboriginal Corporation, held 383 residents including 145 children. The NT rejected a Commonwealth offer to share the purchase; Minister McCarthy said it objected because it was Aboriginal-run. Residents moved to Batchelor, about 100 km away.
state_account: Could not agree a fair price with the owner.

title: Flood evacuations to Darwin
detail: About 1,000 people in evacuation centres in March; police raised their 'community safety posture' around centres. Evacuees' emergency payments were quarantined until they returned.

title: Papunya tenants sue over heat
detail: Australia's first case over housing unsafe in extreme heat.

title: Armed Police Public Safety Officers
detail: 34 public housing and 22 transit officers armed and placed under police command; first squad deployed on Operation Ventura.

title: Operation Ventura (Palmerston)
detail: Over eight weeks: 118 arrests, 375 Banned Drinker Orders, 2,335 move-ons by week six, 76 protective custody apprehensions; targeted illegal camping and public housing.

title: 1 in 17 First Nations Territorians live with RHD or ARF history
detail: At 31 December 2024; 4,597 on the register; highest in Barkly.

title: Parole rehab (COMMIT) cut
detail: $2.1M for rehab beds and counselling for people on parole; the Parole Board chair said it 'will once again add to the very high rates of incarceration of Aboriginal people' (date to confirm).

title: Genocide prosecution needs the Attorney-General
detail: A court held Uncle Robbie Thorpe's attempted genocide prosecution of King Charles would need the Attorney-General's consent.

title: Project Mangma stalled
detail: Eric Fejo's five-week cultural diversion program, built over 14 months with Larrakia ceremony-ground authority and support from police, defence and the Chief Judge.

title: Anindilyakwa justice on Groote Eylandt
detail: An Anindilyakwa-led justice program linked to an 88% fall in crime, underpinned by housing.
source_title: Justice not Jails, Submission 282, racism inquiry (2026)

title: Justice not Jails Drivers Network
detail: Volunteers drive families to visit children at Holtze.
source_title: Justice not Jails, Submission 282, racism inquiry (2026)

title: Eric Fejo: 85% never see daylight again
detail: A former prison officer of ten years says 18-year-olds once had an 8-12% chance of returning or dying by suicide; today he puts it at 85%. Shown beside the official 60.3% (different measures).
